status: declared by the pull request that closes #453, before any score: the three candidates, the primary test, the multiple-comparison rule, the calendar, the turning-point probability model and its threshold are fixed here and nothing is tuned on a scored day
decides: nothing: no published declaration, record or live pin changes; adopting a variant is Eleonora's decision under docs/decisions/publish-rule.md and, for the live pin, her own attested approval (docs/decisions/live-pin.md)

references.published: the published distribution model: the 'published' side of final_test_preregistration.CRPS_COMMAND (gbm, the CRPS_FEATURES, conformal_pid_nested calibration, minimum history 61, refit every 21 scored days, the five quantile levels)
references.twin: published_gbm_direct of metadata/direct_pairs_twin.json (#450): the same, trained on direct pairs
references.persistence: as-of persistence, the 'persistence' side of the same command

scoring.note: scored days are before 2026-01-01 (docs/decisions/lockbox.md); the 2026 window and the blind tier are not looked at; the panel is cut at 2025-12-31 before any fit

blend_equal.rule: at each scored day, the equal-weight average of the published model's and the twin's UNCALIBRATED quantile vectors at each of the five levels, then the published online calibration (conformal_pid_nested, the same factory, its constants and its scorecaster unchanged) applied to the averaged vector
blend_equal.fitted: both gradient-boosted fits are made at the published refit blocks, from the same training frame; nothing else is fitted
blend_equal.note: an average of two non-crossing vectors does not cross; the calibration sees one vector, as it does for the published model

calendar_switch.rule: the twin's calibrated forecast on a flagged day and the published model's calibrated forecast on every other day
calendar_switch.flag: a scored day is flagged when any of the four indicators of recalibration.scorecaster_calendar (the calendar the published calibration already uses, at horizon 1) is 1 for it: month_end (days_to_month_end within the month-end window of metadata/evaluation_splits.json), quarter_end, tax_date (corporate tax dates), coupon_settlement (treasury_settlement_coupons > 0, the mid-month and month-end Treasury coupon settlement dates, public at the decision instant)
calendar_switch.ex_ante: every indicator is read at the scored day's decision instant by the scorecaster's own rule and refused (LookAheadError) when not yet public

predicted_turn_switch.rule: the twin's calibrated forecast when the predicted turning-point probability of the scored day is at least 0.5, the published model's otherwise
predicted_turn_switch.label: a day D is a turning point under the definition of #445 (metadata/nowcast.json): SOFR - IORB moved by at least 2 bp into it from the day before and at least 2 bp the other way out of it to the day after. The label of D is known only from the spread of D+1
features: spread_bps of the as-of row (the row the published model reads for the scored day, two rows before it)
that spread minus the spread one row earlier
the absolute value of that change
the standard deviation of the five spreads up to and including the as-of row
the four scorecaster calendar indicators of the scored day, read at its decision instant
predicted_turn_switch.model: sklearn LogisticRegression (l2, C = 1.0, lbfgs, max_iter 1000) on features standardised by the training window's mean and standard deviation; nothing else is set
predicted_turn_switch.fit: walk-forward, refitted at the first scored day of each block of 21 scored days (the published refit blocks), on the days D whose label was public at that day's decision instant, that is whose next day's spread is at or before the block's first as-of row, from the first day with five earlier spreads; labels of later days are never used
predicted_turn_switch.degenerate: when the training window has fewer than 10 turning points or only one class, the probability is the training base rate
predicted_turn_switch.never_tuned: the threshold, the C, the feature list and the window are not changed after any score

test.primary: the paired per-day gain CRPS(published) - CRPS(candidate) over every scored day, for each candidate: mean and 90% stationary-bootstrap interval (block length 2, 2000 replications, level 0.90, seed 453, the published CRPS cell's rule); all three candidates are read off the same resamples
test.multiple_comparison: Holm across the three candidates at one-sided alpha 0.05 (the lower end of the 90% interval). One-sided p of a candidate = (1 + the number of resamples whose mean gain is <= 0) / (1 + 2000). Candidates are ranked by p, ties in the order blend_equal, calendar_switch, predicted_turn_switch. The candidate of rank r has Holm-adjusted lower bound = the alpha/(3 - r + 1) quantile of its resampled mean gains. A candidate is better than the published model when its own and every earlier-ranked candidate's Holm-adjusted lower bound is above 0; worse when its 90% upper bound is below 0; otherwise there is no difference

secondary: each candidate's gain over the published model, with a 90% interval, split by the declared regimes, by the pressure-day types of metadata/evaluation_splits.json, on turning-point days (the #445 definition) and the other days, and on month-end days (the month_end indicator) and the other days
the gain over as-of persistence: CRPS(persistence) - CRPS(model) for each candidate, the published model and the twin, and each candidate's minus the published model's

the best cross-correlation lag of the forecast median with the actual spread, the integer k in -3..5 at which the Pearson correlation of the median of day T with the actual spread of day T-k is highest (the smaller k in a tie), for each candidate, all days and by regime
the share of scored days whose actual spread lies inside the 50% band [q25, q75] and the 90% band [q05, q95], by regime, for each candidate

for predicted_turn_switch: the number of days the switch fires, its hit rate on actual turning-point days (fired and a turning point, over turning-point days), and its precision (fired and a turning point, over fired days)

pressure.rule: published_v1 is a judge candidate (metadata/pressure_judge/candidates/published_v1.json), so each variant's implied P(spread > threshold) is added as a judge candidate in its own file under metadata/pressure_judge/candidates/ (#446) and its tier-1 row is reported: episodes warned at lead >= 1 and false alarms per episode
pressure.implementation: the pressure candidates' construction is declared in an amendment of this file, committed before any pressure score and after the CRPS scores of this directive; it changes no CRPS candidate

if_better: a needs-eleonora issue titled "Publish? Turning-point variant (#453)" carries the evidence table; no published figure moves in the pull request
